verses.text: The high priest asked, “Is what they’re saying true?”
Stephen answered, “Brothers and fathers, hear me out. The glorious God appeared to our ancestor Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran.
God told him, ‘Leave your country and your relatives. Go to the land I will show you.’
So Abraham left the Chaldean country and settled in Haran. After his father died, God brought him to this land where you now live.
God gave him no inheritance here—not even a small patch to stand on. But God promised to give this land to him and his descendants, even though Abraham had no child yet.
God told him his descendants would live as foreigners in another country. They would be enslaved and mistreated for four hundred years.
God said, ‘I will judge the nation that enslaves them. Afterward, they will leave that country and worship me here.’
Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision. Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs.
“The patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him into Egypt. But God was with Joseph.
God rescued him from all his troubles and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Pharaoh made him governor over Egypt and his whole household.
Then famine and great hardship hit all Egypt and Canaan. Our ancestors couldn’t find food.
When Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt, he sent our ancestors there for the first time.
On their second trip, Joseph revealed who he was to his brothers, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph’s family.
Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all their relatives—seventy-five people altogether.
Jacob went down to Egypt. He died there, as did our ancestors.
Their bodies were brought back to Shechem and laid in the tomb Abraham had bought with silver from Hamor’s sons in Shechem.
“As the time drew near for God to fulfill the promise he had sworn to Abraham, our people grew and multiplied in Egypt.
Then a different king came to power, one who knew nothing about Joseph.
He took advantage of our people, mistreated our ancestors, and forced them to abandon their babies so they wouldn’t survive.
At that time Moses was born. He was beautiful in God’s sight, and for three months he was cared for in his father’s home.
When he was abandoned, Pharaoh’s daughter took him in and raised him as her own son.
Moses was trained in all the wisdom of the Egyptians. He was powerful in his words and actions.
When he was forty, he decided to visit his own people, the Israelites.
He saw one of them being mistreated, stepped in to defend him, and struck down the Egyptian who was hurting him.
Moses thought his people would understand that God was using him to rescue them. They didn’t understand.
“The next day, Moses came across two Israelites fighting. He tried to make peace between them: ‘You’re brothers! Why are you hurting each other?’
But the man who was hurting his neighbor shoved Moses aside and said, ‘Who made you our ruler and judge?
Are you going to kill me like you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’
When Moses heard that, he fled. He lived as a foreigner in Midian, where he became the father of two sons.
“Forty years later, an angel appeared to Moses in the wilderness near Mount Sinai, in the flame of a burning bush.
Moses was amazed by what he saw. As he came closer to look, the Lord’s voice spoke to him:
‘I am the God of your ancestors—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Moses trembled and didn’t dare look.
The Lord told him, ‘Take off your sandals. The ground you’re standing on is holy.
I have seen how my people are suffering in Egypt. I have heard their groans, and I have come to rescue them. Now come—I’m sending you to Egypt.’
“This is the same Moses they had rejected when they asked, ‘Who made you ruler and judge?’ God sent him as both ruler and rescuer, through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
Moses led them out. He performed wonders and signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
This is the Moses who told the Israelites, ‘God will raise up a prophet for you from among your own people, like me.’
Moses was with our ancestors in the wilderness assembly, with the angel who spoke to him at Mount Sinai. He received living words from God to pass on to us.
But our ancestors refused to obey him. They rejected Moses and, in their hearts, turned back toward Egypt.
They told Aaron, ‘Make gods to lead us. We don’t know what happened to this Moses who brought us out of Egypt.’
They made a calf in those days, offered sacrifices to the idol, and celebrated what their own hands had made.
“So God turned away from them and let them serve the heavenly bodies. As the prophets’ book says: ‘People of Israel, did you bring me offerings and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness?
You carried the shrine of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan—the idols you made to worship. So I will send you away beyond Babylon.’
“Our ancestors had the tent of the covenant in the wilderness. God had told Moses to make it according to the pattern he had seen.
Our ancestors brought it with them under Joshua when they took possession of the lands of the nations God drove out before them. It remained there until David’s time.
David found favor with God and asked for a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
But Solomon built a house for him.
Still, the Most High doesn’t live in houses built by human hands. As the prophet says:
‘Heaven is my throne, and the earth is a footrest for my feet. What kind of house could you build for me?’ says the Lord. ‘Where could I rest?
Didn’t my hand make all these things?’
“You stubborn people! Your hearts and ears are uncircumcised. You always resist the Holy Spirit, just like your ancestors did.
Which prophet did your ancestors not persecute? They killed those who announced the coming of the Righteous One. And now you have betrayed and murdered him.
You received the Law, delivered through angels, but you haven’t kept it!”
When the council heard this, it cut them to the heart, and they ground their teeth at Stephen.
But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked steadily up to heaven. He saw God’s glory, and Jesus standing at God’s right hand.
He said, “Look! I see heaven opened, and the Son of Man standing at God’s right hand!”
They shouted at the top of their voices, covered their ears, and rushed at him together.
They dragged him out of the city and stoned him. The witnesses left their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.
As they stoned Stephen, he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!”
He knelt down and called out loudly, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them!” After saying this, he fell asleep.
